title: Nothing Cools But the Price

mood.label: Uneasy thaw 🌥️
mood.summary: A 48 — the top of the mixed band — because the one thing that actually eased was the price of oil: talks with Tehran opened the day after the strike was called off, Brent slid off ninety, Pacific fuel caps came down for the first time since April — while Gaza took another tower, Russia and Ukraine killed fourteen more between them, artillery returned to Sheraro, Spokane lost six hundred houses to a fire with no line around it, Yangsan hit 42.5C on its fifth day above forty, and Cuba's grid failed again: a thaw at one edge of a summer that is still burning everywhere else.

style.genre: motorik krautrock — a four-on-the-floor RolandTR707 kit under 16th hats and a rotated 3-of-8 rim, running straight ahead and never arriving; a GM clavinet holding a relentless sixteenth ostinato as the engine of the thing, a VCSL drawbar organ breathing chords through a 14-cycle filter, a Rhodes-ish GM electric piano carrying the topline and a bowed string swell underneath, an upright GM acoustic bass pumping eighths on the roots with a sine sub below. E melodic minor throughout, so the raised C# and D# keep lighting the minor from inside — brightness that never changes the mode, which is exactly what a day of falling oil prices did to a burning summer. A deliberate move away from the post-punk guitar, sax, balafon, harp, flute and piano-ballad palettes of the last eight days, and a fifth up from yesterday's A

lines: He called the bombers back on Saturday and sat down with Tehran on Monday;
somewhere in Oman they're drawing up who gets to hold the strait.
Brent slid off ninety, the futures found their feet, the Sensex opened seven hundred up,
and in Viti Levu the diesel came down thirteen and seven-tenths — first easier week since April.
But nothing cools but the price.
Not Yangsan at forty-two point five, fifth day running over forty;
not the ridge above Spokane — six hundred houses gone, no line around it, sixty-five thousand out on the road.
The oil comes down. The summer doesn't. That's the thaw, and that's the price.
Abdullah, and Abeer who was carrying, and Azzam who was five —
one apartment in the Al-Sousi Tower, one morning, one raid, one line in the count.
A thirteen-year-old by a playground in Belgorod; nothing left to shoot the missiles down.
Guns again near Sheraro, where three years of quiet had been holding, and ten million Cubans in the dark.
Somewhere they built a crystal out of time itself
and halved what light gives up in passing.
Somewhere off Madura they are still counting forty-one,
and the water is very calm this morning, and the water is very wide.
